message:
Add flake build file

This commit adds a flake.nix build file, it can be used for three
things:

Build `headscale` from local or straight from git:

nix build
or
nix build github:juanfont/headscale

Run and Build `headscale` from local or straight from git:

nix run
or
nix run github:juanfont/headscale

Set up a development environment including all our tools,
- linters
- protobuf tooling
- compilers

nix develop

Add option to build docker image

This commit adds dockerbuild to flakes.nix:

```
nix build .#headscale-docker
```

This uses the Nix infra to build and _does not_ use Dockerfile.

It currently works on Linux (no macOS)

body: I see this being used as a reproducible build system going forward, migrating off the Dockerfile and using this.

body:
> Does this mean we should have a Nix computer on hand to dev on headscale in the future? 

No, Nix by itself is a language/build system/package manager in this content and can be installed on Linux and macOS machines like other build system, for example Bazel (and some parts of Make).

> Will the Docker container will still be built? 

Yes, this PR just makes it _possible_ to build it with docker, it does not transition the build. We _might_ want to do it in the future to consolidate the build and reuse the same build process fo the binary.

> Sorry for the eventually noob question I don't know nix at all.

No worries, it is a learning process. 

The main goal here is to start testing it, and it solves quite a bit of headaches, were we can guarantee that the binary can be built across machines as long as they use nix, since nix guarantees that we have the same Go compiler, the same gRPC toolkit and so on, on each machine.
